headline: Southborough boards weighed major school facility investments and debated contentious CPA-funded projects ahead of the October Special Town Meeting.
synopsis: Ahead of the October Special Town Meeting, municipal boards prepared recommendations on warrant articles, including water extensions near the Parkerville landfill and contentious Community Preservation Act requests for a Peninsula Trail bridge and golf course irrigation. The Elementary School Building Committee moved to advance a $38 million addition-renovation plan for Margaret A. Neary Elementary School after learning that a $15 million baseline upgrade would be largely consumed by mandatory building code triggers. Meanwhile, the school district reported that Neary's ongoing roof replacement is nearly complete and expected to return roughly $2 million in unspent funds to the town. Regional school officials identified an upcoming $800,000 drop in high school debt service and evaluated employee healthcare changes to contain FY28 costs. The Southborough School Committee also approved contract amendments aligning local teacher salaries with Algonquin Regional High School starting in 2027.

top_items.title: Building committee advances $38 million Neary addition-renovation plan
top_items.why: Architects revealed a $15 million baseline upgrade would leave just $5.8 million for direct construction after mandatory code triggers, prompting the committee to pursue a $38 million modernization.
top_items.body: Tappé Architects presented a detailed analysis showing that after subtracting soft costs, contingencies, and the ongoing roof project, a $15 million baseline upgrade leaves only $5.8 million for construction. Because project expenditures would exceed one-third of the building's value, state building codes mandate full sprinkler installation and extensive accessibility modifications, leaving no funds for boilers, univent replacements, or educational improvements. The committee concluded the baseline scope fails to meet fundamental needs and scheduled a vote to authorize schematic designs and cost models for the $38 million addition and renovation option ahead of the March 2027 Annual Town Meeting.

top_items.title: Neary School roof project anticipates returning nearly $2M surplus
top_items.why: District officials reported the roof replacement is nearly 90 percent complete, on schedule, and poised to leave nearly $2 million unspent from its $4.5 million appropriation.
top_items.body: The Margaret A. Neary Elementary School roof replacement is wrapping up ahead of mid-November demobilization, with work nearly 90 percent finished. School administrators confirmed to the School Committee that the project achieved substantial savings, allowing nearly $2 million of the voter-approved $4.5 million borrowing authorization to be returned to the town. Progress was also reported on the Trottier Middle School roof project design and flooring evaluations at Finn School.

top_items.title: Board split deepens over Peninsula Trail footbridge CPA funding
top_items.why: The Community Preservation Committee voted 3-2 to send a $217,318 funding request to Special Town Meeting, despite opposition from the Select Board and Advisory Committee.
top_items.body: The Community Preservation Committee rejected scaling back Article 4 or cutting its contingency, voting 3-2 to present the article as written to Special Town Meeting. The measure requests $217,318 in additional CPA funds to build a 65-foot prefabricated pedestrian bridge along Route 30, bringing the total project cost to $428,550. While trail advocates emphasize pedestrian safety and regional connectivity, the Advisory Committee unanimously opposed the measure, citing excessive costs of roughly $5,000 per linear foot.

top_items.title: Expiring debt to yield $800,000 net regional school debt reduction
top_items.why: Regional school subcommittees learned that the expiration of 2004 high school bonds will significantly lower debt service after FY27, even with new borrowing for athletic facilities.
top_items.body: Subcommittees of the Northborough-Southborough Regional School Committee reviewed Algonquin Regional High School's FY28 capital plan and budget outlook. Officials corrected a presentation arithmetic error to confirm that five FY28 capital projects total approximately $460,000. Crucially, the original 2004 high school renovation debt is scheduled to expire at the end of FY27, which administrators project will produce an estimated $800,000 net reduction in debt service. Subcommittees also explored restructuring employee health insurance deductibles to mirror state plans, potentially yielding $600,000 in regional savings.

top_items.title: Debate continues on golf course irrigation Town Meeting article
top_items.why: The Golf Committee decided to keep its Special Town Meeting article intact, seeking over $433,000 in new CPA money despite unanimous Advisory Committee opposition.
top_items.body: The Golf Committee agreed to present Article 3 to Special Town Meeting as written without seeking floor amendments or splitting the question. The article seeks to extend sunset deadlines on $550,000 in past CPA funds and authorize an additional $433,546 in CPA money, alongside $100,000 from the golf course revolving fund, for an irrigation system replacement. The Advisory Committee voted against the article, contending that the municipal course should be self-funding rather than relying on taxpayer-funded CPA grants.

top_items.title: School Committee amends teacher contract to match Algonquin pay
top_items.why: The School Committee approved contract amendments for Southborough Teachers Association Unit A that revise retirement incentives and match high school salary schedules starting July 2027.
top_items.body: Following an executive session, the Southborough School Committee voted 5-0 in open session to approve contract amendments to Articles 22 and 29 of the collective bargaining agreement with Southborough Teachers Association Unit A. The revisions update the district's retirement incentive program and align Southborough elementary teacher salaries with the Algonquin Regional Teachers Association salary schedule effective July 1, 2027.

top_items.title: Advisory backs $240,000 water connection near Parkerville landfill
top_items.why: The Advisory Committee voted 6-0 to recommend Article 7, using water retained earnings to connect two homes near the landfill to municipal water.
top_items.body: The Advisory Committee voted unanimously to recommend approval of Warrant Article 7 for the Special Town Meeting. The measure appropriates $240,000 from water retained earnings to extend a water main and connect two residential properties near the Parkerville Road landfill to town water. Committee members confirmed that the town will pay for the service connections from the street directly into the homes to resolve private well contamination concerns and avoid state-mandated PFAS testing.
